label: OF3 code + Anthropic kit `big` (fused kernels + offload at every size), no templates, openbind weights
tag: OF3 code / kit big / openbind weights
notes: mode big with OPENFOLD3_OB0_OPT_REACH_GATE=none (launcher.env): the kit's reach gate never engages, so at
every size the trunk keeps fast's fused pair kernels and big's offload units (row-block triangle
multiplication from a pinned host snapshot, template and recycling features on the host, chunked
confidence heads). This is exactly what of3kit_big runs BELOW 4500 tokens; the only change is that it
does not switch to the streamed trunk at 4500.
WHY. The reach gate is a per-card table tuned for an 80 GB H100 (modes.REACH_GATE_BY_CARD), where the
fused path stops fitting around 4500 tokens; the streamed trunk it switches to measured ~26x slower here
(of3kit_big at 4500: a 72 min trunk). This card has 96 GB, and of3kit_big's memory below the gate was
36.4 / 41.7 / 48.7 GiB at 3000 / 3500 / 4000 tokens -- extrapolated with N^2 growth, ~60 GiB in the
trunk and ~80 GiB at the sampler peak for the 5120-token pools of the production scheme. Whether that
fits is what this arm measures; if it does, the pooled scheme gets fast's kernels at about 1.25x fast's
time, roughly 1.5x faster than the AlphaFold3 code at that size. If it does not, the boundary is one
gpu_oom row, minutes, not hours.

MEASURED 2026-09-22 (job 14837078, RTX PRO 6000, 8 x 16 GB host): ok through 6000 tokens -- 5000: 510 s at 57.2 GiB; 5500: 628 s at 68.8 GiB; 6000: 773 s at 81.5 GiB -- gpu_oom at 6500 (91 GiB). Host anonymous memory peaked at 71 GB at 6000 tokens, so the 128 GB request was needed. Against the AlphaFold3 code on the same pools: 835 s at 5000 and 1001 s at 5500, i.e. this arm is 1.6x faster at the production scheme's size and reaches 500 tokens further (the AF3 code fails at 6000).
levers_off=pair_transition as for fast (the fused pair transition refuses on compute capability 12.0).
warmup_runs 1, mem_per_cpu 16g and time 24:00:00 as for of3kit_big; below 4500 this arm duplicates it.
THE GATES COME FROM THE CARD FILE. OF3O_MIN_TOKENS and the reach gate are looked up by
MODEL_OPT_TARGET_GPU, which launcher.kit_config=h100 sets to H100: the gate is 1401 tokens, tuned
for an 80 GB card. This card has 96 GB, so big engages somewhat earlier than it would need to; the
sweep still answers the question it is asked (peak memory and time against size under big) but the
crossover with fast is the H100's, not this card's. OF3O_MIN_TOKENS=<n> in the environment overrides.
levers_off=pair_transition as for fast: the big line carries fast's pair cells below its reach gate
and the fused pair transition refuses on compute capability 12.0 (see of3kit_fast).
big needs pinned host memory for the offloaded pair representation (OF3O_PIN_BUDGET_GB, the kit's
default 600 is a cap, not a reservation); the SLURM block below is the of3 arm's 64 GB. A size that
ends with status cpu_oom rather than gpu_oom wants more mem_per_cpu, not a smaller pool.
Measured 2026-09-21 (job 14777851, RTX PRO 6000, 8 x 8 GB host): ok through 4000 tokens (48.7 GiB peak GPU,
355 s), then killed at 4500 by the HOST OOM killer -- twice, warm-up and recorded run -- with the GPU at
49.7 GiB of 96. So the 64 GB host request, not the card, was the limit: hence mem_per_cpu 16g here.
At 4500 tokens the kit's REACH GATE engages (REACH_GATE_BY_CARD H100 = 4500, from launcher.kit_config):
the fused full-N^2 pair kernels step aside and the trunk runs in row blocks streamed from pinned host
snapshots. Measured cost: one recycle 1,068 s streamed against ~41 s fused at 4000 tokens -- the trunk
alone took 72 min, ~26x slower, with the GPU flat at 20 GiB the whole time. That is the mode doing what
it is for (fast OOMs at 4500 on this card at 91 GiB, so the full-N^2 path genuinely does not fit), but
it means sizes >= 4500 of this arm are a MEMORY curve, not a speed curve; each such size costs ~80 min
per run, x2 with the warm-up, hence time 24:00:00. OPENFOLD3_OB0_OPT_REACH_GATE=<n> in the environment
moves the gate. On this 96 GB card there IS a reason to: see of3kit_big_reachoff_templateoff.json.
The OpenFold3 CODEBASE on the openbind weights, launched through Anthropic's `openfold3_ob0`
optimization kit (github.com/anthropics/uplifting-biomolecular-modeling, Apache-2.0, released
2026-09-17 as a reference release that is not maintained). The kit is NOT vendored: launcher.kit_dir
names a clone at launcher.kit_commit, and profiling/setup_kit_env.sh builds everything the launcher
block names. engine stays `of3`: same codebase family, same PyTorch memory counter, same of3_pool
queries as of3_openbind_templateoff; only the launcher differs.
launcher.kit_config: the kit's per-card file that is SOURCED for its environment bootstrap. The kit
ships h100|a100|h200|b200|b300 and nothing for this GPU (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, compute capability
12.0). The card files differ in exactly one functional line, MODEL_OPT_TARGET_GPU, which only the
`big` mode's two size gates consume; for off/exact/fast the kernel tables are resolved from the real
compute capability at run time (cc 12.0 has no tuned rows and gets the kit's safe settings, which
it reports on its own). h100 is the kit's tested reference and is used for that reason only.
launcher.cuda_home / ld_library_path: two host workarounds, explained in profiling/setup_kit_env.sh
(deviations 2 and 3). Override any launcher path without editing this file: AF3OF3_KIT_DIR,
AF3OF3_KIT_ENV, AF3OF3_KIT_CUDA_HOME, AF3OF3_KIT_LD; the checkpoint via AF3OF3_OF3_CKPT as for of3.
warmup_runs 1: each size is run once untimed before the recorded run. The kit compiles Triton
kernels per tensor shape inside the timed loop (its README: compare modes on a second run), and
stock's Triton kernels autotune per shape too, so all three kit arms warm equally. Default 0 leaves
every other arm as it was.
use_templates=false for the same reason as the of3 arm: the converted queries carry none.
Recycles: OpenFold3's fixed 3, as for of3. Samples and seed as the other arms.
